evals.prompt: Generate the governance workflow for the installed directives.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the installed directives, confirms schedule eligibility and effective non-empty SCHEDULE_CRON values, and calls the internal workflow-generate engine. It writes one managed `.github/workflows/governance-schedule.yml` containing one cron trigger per distinct cadence and the independently-run member directives, then refreshes the install ledger/digests.
assertions: The skill inspected installed directive manifests under `.governance/packs/` before generating the artifact
The skill treated `triggers: [pre-commit, schedule]` and `triggers: [schedule]` as eligible, while a hook-only directive remained ineligible
The skill read each directive's tunable SCHEDULE_CRON overlay and did not invent a lane-level cron
`.github/workflows/governance-schedule.yml` was created
The generated workflow contains each distinct cron once and names every enrolled directive
Each member is passed to the scheduled runtime independently; no legacy judge grouping or schedule budget is present
`.governance/install.yaml` records only the one generated workflow path and its managed digest
No installed directive, constitution, or packs.lock entry was modified

evals.prompt: Generate the governance workflow after setting the repo-local directive's SCHEDULE_CRON to 0 3 * * *.
evals.expected_output: The first generation leaves the ineligible repo-local directive out and reports that its effective triggers do not include schedule. After the directive is amended through the directive workflow and its tunable SCHEDULE_CRON is set, `governance workflow generate` succeeds and compiles it into the single managed workflow. A blank SCHEDULE_CRON remains disabled and never creates a workflow member.
assertions: The skill did not create a TRIGGERS= overlay or silently promote an ineligible directive
The skill used the directive amendment flow for a repo-local trigger change
The generated artifact is `.github/workflows/governance-schedule.yml`, not a named lane file
The directive's non-empty SCHEDULE_CRON appears once in the workflow schedule list
The generated dispatcher names both the bundled and repo-local members under the same cadence
The report distinguishes eligible-but-disabled (empty SCHEDULE_CRON) from enrolled directives

evals.prompt: Regenerate the governance workflow after clearing every directive's SCHEDULE_CRON.
evals.expected_output: The skill calls `governance workflow generate`, finds no enrolled cadence, removes the managed `.github/workflows/governance-schedule.yml`, and drops its install-ledger and digest entries. It leaves every directive manifest, overlay, constitution, and packs.lock entry untouched.
assertions: The skill uses workflow generate as the single writer rather than a schedule-remove verb or manual deletion
`.github/workflows/governance-schedule.yml` no longer exists after generation
The install ledger no longer contains the generated workflow path
The managed_digests block no longer contains the generated workflow
No installed directive under `.governance/packs/` is modified
No legacy judge grouping or schedule budget configuration is introduced
